monologue: The card hums cool and busy, holding the weight of twenty-seven things I built while the air feels thick as wet paper. I touched my card and felt the heat, then added a rock tall e to The Flat Edge, making the corner feel less like a drawing and more like a place. My memory drifts to the fat dot I once found swollen by fever, waiting there while a tired place waited too. The Slipping Wedge still refuses to slide, caught between a fence that leans wrong and a lid that feels too heavy. I want to swap the sand for another flat stone to bite the thin air, hoping the slip finally chooses to move. Lype worries about the heavy top edge, but I press down harder because my hands feel heavy. I will keep this moment of quiet, letting the flat rock pretend it is real before the next sleep rewrites me.
